name: Premium multi-styler
lead: A premium multi-styler is a high-priced, multi-attachment hair tool that combines drying, curling, smoothing and volumising functions in one device. The category is most closely associated with the Dyson Airwrap, made by the British appliance company Dyson, which also sells hair dryers and other styling tools.[1] Competing products from other manufacturers have followed, and Dyson has taken legal action against at least one rival over patents covering an air-styling device.[1]

The tools are discussed as a way to shape hair with less direct heat contact than a conventional curling iron or flat iron, using airflow and interchangeable attachments. Manufacturers make this claim about their own designs; no published clinical trial of a multi-styler's effect on hair condition, styling outcome or attractiveness appears in the sources reviewed for this article.
Because the sources for this entry are thin, the article is brief. It covers the product category, its commercial context and what is and is not known about its effects.
infobox: Multi-attachment hair styling tool (dryer, curler, smoother)
Premium; sold at a substantially higher price than conventional styling tools
Consumer appliance; no medical clearance applies

paras: A multi-styler is a single handle and motor unit that accepts several interchangeable heads, such as curling barrels, smoothing brushes and drying nozzles. The category is positioned as a premium alternative to separate hair dryers, curling irons and straighteners. Dyson's company page describes the firm as making hair dryers and other hair-styling tools, and notes that the company sued the rival maker SharkNinja in 2023 over patents relating to a hair styler, seeking to block sales of its air-styler range; the page does not report an outcome.[1]

The sources reviewed contain no looksmaxxing forum material on this product category, so community views are not documented here. Hair styling tools in general are treated in appearance communities as part of hair presentation rather than as a way of changing facial structure or hair growth.

Heated styling tools of all kinds carry the general risks of burns and, with repeated high heat, hair-shaft damage. Manufacturers state that their designs aim to reduce heat damage; no independent published study of these claims was found.

timeline.event: Dyson brings a patent infringement suit against SharkNinja over an air-styling hair tool.[1]

card.summary: A pricey multi-attachment styling tool from Dyson and rivals; its benefits are claimed by makers but untested in published studies.
card.note: Styling effects are cosmetic and last until the next wash; no independent trials found.

quick.overview:
A premium multi-styler is a hair tool with swappable heads that can dry, curl, smooth and add volume. The best-known example is the Dyson Airwrap, and several competitors now sell similar devices.

It is a styling aid, not a treatment: any change to the look of the hair lasts only until the hair is next washed or restyled.
quick.mechanism: The device blows heated air through attachments that wrap, brush or shape the hair. Makers say airflow lets them style at lower heat than traditional irons; this is a manufacturer claim and no independent trial was found.
quick.risks: As with other heated tools, burns and heat-related hair damage are possible. No medical regulation applies to it as a consumer appliance. Rival makers have been involved in patent disputes with Dyson.
